messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] p95 inference latency > 3.0s for 5m on cluster r-inference-5. Route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-7b). Possible kernel fallback / batching regression. Auto-ticket created: INC-1851.

irina-oncall: I'm paged. looking at canary nodes now. marco, can you check runtime logs for kernel selector fallbacks? june, any recent rollout to canary?

marco: on it. seeing repeated messages on gpu-12/gpu-13: kernel_selector: fallback -> generic_kernel due to 'sm_arch_mismatch' and then long stalls between token generations. Example: 
```
2026-03-15T20:14:02Z gpu-12 runtime ERROR kernel_selector.cpp:312 fallback to generic_kernel (reason: sm_async_mismatch)
2026-03-15T20:14:02Z gpu-12 runtime WARN kv_cache.cpp:128 eviction triggered, prefix cache miss rate 0.42
2026-03-15T20:14:03Z gpu-12 runtime INFO batching.cpp: queue_depth=1, flush_interval_ms=1200
```
Throughput per replica dropped ~70% in last 10m.

june: confirming we rolled out build r-inference:2026.03.15-canary-7 with experimental kernel-affinity toggle enabled (flag: aggressive_batch_affinity=true). That was targeted to canary only. deploy-bot shows rollout started 2026-03-15T19:58:00Z.

irina-oncall: can we toggle the flag off quickly? this looks like a regression in canary.

deploy-bot: feature flag aggressive_batch_affinity currently: ON for canary (r-inference-5).

june: i'll flip it. doing: `/featureflag set aggressive_batch_affinity canary OFF --why "latency regression"`

deploy-bot: feature flag aggressive_batch_affinity set to OFF for canary by june at 2026-03-15T20:17:44Z.

marco: flag off observed on endpoints, but latency still elevated. I'm seeing kernel fallback count dropping slowly, but batching queue_depth remains tiny. suspect there's leftover kernel cache state or new image introduced a kernel selection path that requires full rollback.

irina-oncall: we need clear mitigation. options: restart canary pods, evict problematic nodes, or rollback image. which is fastest?

marco: quick step: restart canary replicas to clear kernel state and warm up optimized kernels. doing rolling restart on r-inference-5-canary.

ops-bot: initiating rolling restart for r-inference-5-canary (12 replicas) with 30s drain delay.

marco: restarts didn't fully recover throughput; p95 down from 4.2s to ~2.1s but baseline is 0.6s. still unacceptable. logs show a mismatch in compiled kernels vs. runtime capabilities for about 30% of requests; fallback still happening intermittently.

june: given partial recovery, i recommend rollback to previous image revision r-inference:2026.03.10-stable-4 in canary and pause the rollout to prod. we didn't push to prod yet but the release pipeline had staged traffic slices.

irina-oncall: +1 rollback. sam-cs, any customer reports yet? need to know impact.

sam-cs: Support flagged three enterprise customers reporting timeouts and elevated latency for embedded chat. They're on Dedicated but traffic hit the canary model variant via traffic-slicing in the deploy plan. CS notified them and opened tickets. No escalations to legal yet.

june: initiating rollback: `/deploy rollback r-inference-5 canary --to r-inference:2026.03.10-stable-4 --reason "kernel fallback regression"`

deploy-bot: rollback started by june at 2026-03-15T20:35:10Z. Expected canary finish ~4m.

incidents-bot: INC-1851 status: mitigation in progress (rollback). impact: elevated latency, reduced throughput, some timeouts. severity: S2 (customer-facing, partial).

marco: rollback completed. monitoring shows kernel_selector fallback metrics near zero and batching queue_depth back to normal. p95 at 0.65s across canary.

irina-oncall: great. let's keep traffic paused to prod. june, hold rollout until postmortem and validation tests added.

june: will pause deploy pipeline and open a PR with CI tests that reproduce the kernel selection path.

sam-cs: informed affected customers that we rolled back canary and are monitoring; offered interim credits. they're satisfied for now but want root cause.

ryan-oncall: i'm taking handoff at 23:00 UTC. summary for night: incident INC-1851, rollout to canary with aggressive_batch_affinity true caused kernel selector mismatches and high p95. mitigations: feature flag OFF, rolling restart, rollback to stable image. Status:Resolved on canary, traffic to prod paused. Action items: add targeted integration tests to reproduce kernel selection; add alert for kernel_fallback_rate > 0.05 on canary; document rollback playbook.

irina-oncall: handing over to ryan-oncall. brief notes: keep an eye on dedicated customers; if any timeouts reappear, escalate to eng-runtime oncall.

ryan-oncall: ack. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and watch for regressions on gpu-12/gpu-13 metric groups.

incidents-bot: INC-1851 update: incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T20:42:00Z after rollback; monitoring stable for 10m. Postmortem required.

marco: adding to postmortem draft: reproduce run with synthetic workload hitting attention patterns + simulate heterogenous GPU sm_arch profiles. initial hypothesis: new kernel-affinity logic preferred kernels incompatible with certain node driver versions leading to fallback and poor batching behavior.

june: also adding infra note: our canary gating didn't catch kernel_fallback_rate; will add a canary-liveness check to block rollouts if fallback > 1% during first 10m.

sam-cs: closing customer-facing LOE: provide root cause summary once postmortem live.

incidents-bot: INC-1851 status: resolved -> will remain open for postmortem tracking.
